title: Senior Manager, QMS - Manufacturing
text:
Crusoe is on a mission
*to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence*
. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.
 
 
We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.
 
 
We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.
 
 
If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.
 
 
**About This Role:**
The
**Senior Manager, Quality Management Systems (QMS)**
will lead the development, implementation, governance, and continuous improvement of Crusoe's enterprise Quality Management System across multiple manufacturing facilities, supplier operations, subcontractors, and field deployment activities.
 
 
This individual will be responsible for establishing a scalable, standardized, risk-based QMS that enables consistent product quality, manufacturing process control, regulatory and customer compliance, and operational excellence across the organization.
 
 
The role will provide strategic and operational leadership for QMS governance, internal and external audits, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), document and records management, quality processes, compliance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Senior Manager will lead and develop a team of QMS professionals, auditors, and documentation specialists while partnering closely with Product Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Supplier Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Field Quality leadership.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of progressive Quality Management System experience, including substantial people-management experience in complex manufacturing environments. This individual must be capable of translating quality standards and business requirements into practical operating processes that improve manufacturing effectiveness, prevent defects, reduce operational risks, and support organizational growth.
 
 
**The ultimate objective is to establish a proactive, business-enabling QMS that drives consistency, accountability, compliance, and continuous improvement across Crusoe's growing AI Data Center infrastructure manufacturing and deployment ecosystem.**
**What You'll Be Working On:**

* Enterprise QMS Strategy, Governance & Leadership

+ Own and lead the enterprise Quality Management System strategy, architecture, implementation, and continuous improvement.
+ Establish and maintain a scalable QMS aligned with ISO 9001:2015 and applicable customer, regulatory, contractual, and industry requirements.
+ Develop standardized Quality policies, procedures, processes, work instructions, forms, and records applicable across all manufacturing facilities and operational functions.
+ Establish QMS governance, process ownership, accountability matrices, escalation mechanisms, and management review processes.
+ Ensure consistent implementation of Quality Management System requirements across Brighton, Tulsa-1, Tulsa-2, Arvada, Ponchatoula, and other future manufacturing and operational locations.
+ Establish a process-based, risk-oriented approach to quality management rather than a documentation-driven compliance culture.
+ Partner with Quality leadership to establish annual QMS objectives, strategic initiatives, resource plans, and performance targets.
+ Lead QMS maturity assessments and develop roadmaps to strengthen process effectiveness and organizational readiness.
+ Ensure QMS requirements are appropriately integrated into product development, manufacturing, supplier management, and field operations.

* ISO Compliance & Audit Management

+ Own the enterprise internal and external audit program, including audit planning, scheduling, execution, reporting, and follow-up.
+ Maintain organizational readiness for ISO 9001 certification, surveillance audits, recertification audits, and customer or third-party audits.
+ Lead and oversee internal audits across manufacturing, engineering, procurement, supplier quality, production, inspection, testing, and field operations.
+ Ensure audit programs evaluate actual process implementation and effectiveness rather than merely verifying documentation.
+ Manage relationships with external certification bodies, registrars, customer auditors, and regulatory or industry assessment organizations.
+ Establish risk-based audit schedules considering process criticality, historical performance, operational changes, and previous audit findings.
+ Ensure audit findings are appropriately classified, assigned, investigated, corrected, and closed within established timelines.
+ Verify corrective action effectiveness and prevent recurrence of systemic audit findings.
+ Develop and maintain qualified internal auditor resources across multiple facilities and functions.

* CAPA, Nonconformance & Continuous Improvement

+ Establish and govern enterprise-wide CAPA, nonconformance, deviation, and quality escalation processes.
+ Ensure effective root cause analysis using structured methodologies such as 5 Why, Fishbone, 8D, fault tree analysis, and other appropriate problem-solving techniques.
+ Drive accountability for corrective and preventive actions across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, and Operations.
+ Monitor CAPA aging, overdue actions, recurrence rates, effectiveness verification, and systemic trends.
+ Identify recurring process failures, systemic weaknesses, and opportunities for organizational improvement.
+ Establish standardized requirements for nonconformance documentation, containment, disposition, investigation, and closure.
+ Lead cross-functional improvement initiatives that reduce process variation, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and strengthen manufacturing process effectiveness.
+ Ensure lessons learned from internal defects, supplier issues, customer complaints, and field failures are incorporated into the QMS.

* QMS Documentation & Records Management

+ Own enterprise document and records management governance.
+ Establish standardized requirements for document creation, review, approval, release, revision control, distribution, retention, and obsolescence.
+ Ensure controlled management of Quality Manuals, policies, procedures, SOPs, work instructions, inspection plans, test procedures, forms, and quality records.
+ Implement effective document control processes across multiple facilities and functional organizations.
+ Ensure personnel have access to current and approved documentation at the point of use.
+ Establish document ownership and periodic review requirements.
+ Eliminate uncontrolled documentation, obsolete work instructions, inconsistent forms, and duplicate processes.
+ Drive adoption and effective utilization of electronic QMS platforms and digital document management solutions.
+ Ensure objective evidence and records are maintained to demonstrate process conformity and effectiveness.

* Risk Management & Operational Quality Governance

+ Establish enterprise-level Quality risk management processes.
+ Ensure risk-based thinking is incorporated into business processes, product realization, supplier management, manufacturing operations, and field activities.
+ Oversee QMS-related risk assessments and coordinate with functional leaders on DFMEA, PFMEA, process risk assessments, and operational controls.
+ Establish escalation mechanisms for significant Quality risks, process deviations, regulatory concerns, and potential customer impacts.
+ Ensure changes to products, processes, suppliers, equipment, and organizational structures are appropriately evaluated for QMS impact.
+ Drive management review processes that evaluate QMS performance, organizational risks, customer satisfaction, audit results, CAPA effectiveness, and improvement opportunities.

* Multi-Site Standardization & Deployment

+ Establish a consistent enterprise QMS framework while allowing controlled, documented site-specific requirements where necessary.
+ Lead QMS deployment, implementation, and maturity improvement across existing and new manufacturing facilities.
+ Partner with site Quality leaders to ensure standardized processes are effectively implemented and sustained.
+ Conduct periodic site assessments to evaluate QMS effectiveness, process adherence, and compliance maturity.
+ Establish cross-site benchmarking and sharing of best practices.
+ Ensure new manufacturing facilities and acquired or outsourced operations are incorporated into the enterprise QMS framework.
+ Develop standardized QMS deployment and operational readiness plans for new facilities.

* Customer, Supplier & Regulatory Quality Support

+ Partner with Supplier Quality leadership to ensure QMS requirements are incorporated into supplier qualification, supplier audits, corrective actions, and supplier performance management.
+ Ensure subcontractors and outsourced manufacturing partners operate under appropriate Quality requirements and controls.
+ Support customer audits, quality assessments, and contractual compliance requirements.
+ Ensure effective management of customer complaints, quality escapes, and external nonconformances through the enterprise CAPA framework.
+ Partner with Product and Manufacturing Quality to ensure appropriate quality planning and process controls are established.
+ Maintain awareness of applicable industry standards, regulatory requirements, and customer-specific Quality requirements relevant to electrical and mechanical infrastructure manufacturing.

* People Leadership & Organizational Development

+ Build, lead, and develop a high-performing QMS organization.
+ Directly manage QMS personnel, including QMS Leads, Quality Auditors, QMS Documentation Specialists, and other assigned Quality professionals.
+ Establish clear roles, responsibilities, performance expectations, and individual development plans.
+ Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, talent assessments, and succession planning.
+ Develop technical and leadership competencies within the QMS organization.
+ Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.
+ Establish effective working relationships with site Quality leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.
+ Identify resource requirements and develop headcount and organizational plans to support current and future business growth.
+ Mentor and develop future Quality leaders and technical subject matter experts.

* Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Establishing, monitoring, and improving measurable QMS performance indicators, including:

+ QMS Compliance
+ Audit Management
+ CAPA Effectiveness
+ Document Control
+ Multi-Site Standardization
+ Process Effectiveness
+ Organizational Development
+ Customer Quality
+ Continuous Improvement

**What You'll Bring to the Team:**

* Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Industrial Technology, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional Experience:

+ 7+ Years of Dedicated Experience in QMS, plus additional experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Quality, or Quality Assurance.
+ 5+ Years of People Leadership Experience: Including managing and developing Quality professionals and technical teams (these years may overlap with the 10+ above).

* QMS Expertise: Demonstrated experience owning, implementing, and improving enterprise or multi-site Quality Management Systems.
* ISO 9001 Expertise: Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001:2015 requirements and certification processes.
* Core Quality Methodologies: Demonstrated expertise in CAPA, root cause analysis, nonconformance management, and continuous improvement.
* Quality Documentation & Document Control: Experience developing and implementing Quality policies, procedures, SOPs, work instructions, and document control systems.
* Cross-Functional Leadership: Experience managing cross-functional Quality initiatives across Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Supply Chain.
* Risk & Process Management: Strong understanding of risk-based thinking, process management, and operational excellence.
* eQMS Implementation: Experience implementing or administering electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS).
* Influence & Accountability: Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and drive organizational accountability without relying solely on hierarchical authority.
* Communication & Analytical Skills: Excellent written, verbal, analytical, organizational, and presentation skills.
* Travel: Willingness to travel 25–40% of the time, based on business needs.
* Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility; drug and alcohol program participation is required. Must be able to pass a background check.

**Bonus Points:**

* Advanced Education: Master's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations Management, or Business Administration.
* Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Manager (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or equivalent professional credentials.
* Lead Auditor Certification: ISO 9001 Lead Auditor certification.
* Industry Experience: Experience in electrical equipment, switchgear, switchboards, power distribution, mechanical assemblies, data center infrastructure, aerospace, automotive, energy, or other complex manufacturing industries.
* Industry Standards: Familiarity with UL 891, UL 508, applicable IEC, IEEE, NEMA, NFPA, and other relevant industry standards.
* Multi-Site QMS Deployment: Experience managing QMS deployment across multiple manufacturing facilities and outsourced manufacturing operations.
* Digital Quality Systems: Experience with digital QMS platforms, ERP integration, document management, and quality analytics.
* Lean & Six Sigma: Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and operational excellence methodologies.
* NPI & Scale-Up: Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), manufacturing scale-up, and new facility launches.

**Benefits:**

* Competitive compensation and equity packages
* Restricted Stock Units
* Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs
* Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance
* Employer contributions to HSA account
* Paid parental leave
* Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability
* Professional development & tuition reimbursement
* Mental health & wellness support
* Commuter benefits (parking & transit)
* Cell phone stipend
* 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary
* Volunteer time off
* Global travel insurance & emergency assistance
* Daily meals allowance
* Additional perks & programs specific to location

**Compensation:**
Compensation will be paid in the range of $190,000 - $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
 
 
Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.
